=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Positions

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package shifts almost all known risk to the Buyer. Of the roughly AUD 4.13m of quantified known exposures, none is covered by a specific indemnity, price adjustment, or condition. The general warranty regime then reduces what the Buyer can recover for anything else, and the Seller's "knowledge" and "data room disclosure" clauses would exclude claims for the very issues Wattlebridge has now identified. We should not accept the package as drafted.

Caveat: I have reviewed the Seller's update summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA. Clause references below are to the Seller's numbering, and each point needs checking against the actual drafting.

---

## 1. The core structural problem: knowledge and disclosure

Several Seller positions work together and should be read as a whole:

- **General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2; Schedule 7):** The Seller discloses "every fact... contained or referred to" in the data room, plus the Accounts and public registers. This would disclose almost anything against any warranty. It is also vague, since "referred to" can be read to cover documents the Buyer never reviewed.
- **Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3):** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. "Discoverable" is a very wide standard, and "advisers" would include the Buyer's own DD team.
- **Exclusive remedy and non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5):** These apply to "all Claims of any nature", including fraud.

**Why this matters:** Wattlebridge has now identified the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonus, privacy, and supplier issues. Under the Seller's drafting, once known, they are excluded from warranty claims, and the general disclosure makes further matters hard to claim too. That leaves the Buyer with no recourse for issues it has already flagged. Known issues must be dealt with through specific mechanisms (price, conditions, specific indemnities, retentions), not through warranties.

**Push back:**
- Delete general disclosure of the data room and public registers. Require specific disclosure against specific warranties, with documents fairly disclosed in reasonable detail.
- Delete the "knowledge" and "discoverable" limb of 8.3, or limit it to actual, written knowledge of specific matters that the Buyer's deal team has documented.
- Carve out fraud from all limitations, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance clauses.
- Make clear that known matters are covered by specific indemnities, which apply regardless of Buyer knowledge.

---

## 2. Liability caps, thresholds and time limits (Clauses 12.1–12.3, 13)

| Term | Seller position | Assessment | Ask |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) | Within the range commonly seen for general warranties, so not unusual in itself. | Accept only if fundamental, tax and specific indemnities sit outside it. Consider 25–30% if DD findings continue to grow. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | Acceptable on a DD record of this size, but the threshold should be tested against aggregated related claims, not each claim separately. | Aggregate related claims. Confirm the de minimis is not drafted to exclude the whole claim. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | "Excess only" (deductible) is worse for Buyer than a tipping basket (first-dollar). The wording "once aggregate claims exceed" is ambiguous. | Tipping basket, or deductible at no more than 0.5–1% of price. Clarify the mechanics with worked examples. |
| General time limit (12.3) | 18 months | Short for a business with open tax, IP, and privacy exposure. | 36 months general. Tax claims to run until 60 days after the ATO period closes. |
| Universal limitation (13) | Any limit applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise | This would apply the general cap and time limit to everything. | Reject. Fundamentals, title, tax, and fraud need separate treatment. |

Note that the Seller's "all Claims" approach converts a negotiating point into a structural one. The Buyer should insist on a clear list of claim categories with their own caps and time limits.

---

## 3. Fundamental and title warranties

The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."

This is a material departure. Title and capacity are the core of what the Buyer is buying. If the Seller does not own the shares, the Buyer has no business. Claims for title should be:
- capped at the full purchase price (AUD 24m), not at AUD 4.8m;
- subject to a longer time limit, ideally the statutory limitation period;
- outside the basket and de minimis.

**Title support (Disclosure Letter 10; Seller update):** The Seller relies on the share register at DD-012 showing Harbourglass as the holder of 100% of the shares. The register confirms the Seller's position, but it is not verification. The Buyer should obtain:
- ASIC company extract and current register;
- evidence of chain of title for all issued shares (share transfer history and any dilutive issues);
- confirmation of no encumbrances, options, or convertible instruments;
- PPSR search results against the Seller and the Company.

---

## 4. Known issues: specific pushback

### 4.1 Bluefen (about 30% of revenue; ~AUD 3.6m FY26)
**Seller position:** Consent "addressed". Seller will use reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

**Problems:**
- The Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms no final written consent exists and that the conditions under clause 11.3 are unsatisfied. The update contradicts this.
- A "reasonable endeavours" obligation does not deliver the consent.
- "Delivery of written consent" may not mean consent on the conditions in 11.3 has been satisfied.

**Push back:**
- Make an unconditional Bluefen consent, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived in writing, a condition precedent to Completion, with a Buyer right to terminate if not satisfied by a long-stop date.
- If the Buyer elects to complete without it, require a specific indemnity and price adjustment or retention for loss of the Bluefen revenue.
- Obtain Bluefen's written confirmation of the conditions and the terms of consent.

### 4.2 Riverlark Bank facility (~AUD 3.2m)
**Seller position:** The facility will be "addressed by a release to be provided following Completion."

**Problems:**
- The price is described as debt-free/cash-free. Debt should therefore be deducted from the price and repaid at Completion from the funds flow, not released afterwards.
- Disclosure Letter item 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and the discharge of security (clause 9.2) is not provided.
- A post-completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with a secured lender's security over its assets, with the Seller holding the cash.

**Push back:**
- Require a payoff letter from Riverlark and executed discharge documents (including PPSR discharge) delivered at Completion.
- Repay the facility out of the Seller's proceeds through the funds flow, with the amount deducted from the price.
- Confirm the funds flow actually deducts AUD 3.2m (plus accrued interest and break costs). The Seller's statement that the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" needs to be checked line by line.

### 4.3 Ironquay Development Studio (SOW3 IP and payment)
**Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000 open) and is "adequate."

**Problems:**
- The DD-004 clause 7.3 condition means SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid. Unpaid, the Company may not own the IP it relies on.
- No receipt or confirmatory IP assignment is in the data room.
- The indemnity covers only the payment itself, not IP ownership, third-party claims, or costs of re-creating the materials.

**Push back:**
- Require the Seller to pay the AUD 180,000 before Completion, or deduct it from the price as a debt-like item.
- Obtain a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay covering all SOW3 materials, delivered at Completion.
- Replace the limited indemnity with a specific indemnity covering all Ironquay matters, including IP ownership, third-party claims, and enforcement costs, outside the basket and cap, with its own time limit.

### 4.4 Employee Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000)
**Seller position:** The bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow.

**Problems:**
- The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment. If they are payable by the Company after Completion, the Buyer bears them.
- The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation, or other on-costs apply. Payroll tax in NSW and superannuation guarantee would add a material amount on top of AUD 420,000. Please verify the current rates and thresholds.

**Push back:**
- Treat all Completion bonuses, plus employer on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, and any related taxes), as debt-like items deducted from the price, or require the Seller to pay them through payroll before Completion.
- Obtain the employment and bonus documents and confirm the conditions.

### 4.5 Privacy / data export incident (DD-006)
**Seller position:** A "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material."

**Problems:**
- The material may contain about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles, and activity timestamps.
- Whether unauthorised access occurred, the exact scope, and whether notification obligations apply are all unknown.
- If it is an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), the Company may need to notify the OAIC and affected individuals, with regulatory and reputational exposure. This needs urgent privacy advice; I have not reviewed the facts against the current statutory test.
- The disclosure does not characterise the matter or estimate loss.

**Push back:**
- Require a specific indemnity for all losses arising from the incident (investigation, notification, regulatory action, remediation, third-party claims), outside the basket and general cap.
- Require the Seller to fund the forensic investigation before Completion, or give the Buyer control over it post-Completion with Seller cooperation.
- Consider a retention or escrow sized to the potential exposure until the matter is resolved.
- Require full investigation records and any correspondence with regulators or affected persons.

### 4.6 Supplier renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate)
**Seller position:** Ordinary course operating costs.

**Problems:**
- Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, read together, may be a multi-year commitment that should be reflected in price or treated as a debt-like item.
- The disclosure does not say whether the contracts are terminable, accrued, or unavoidable.

**Push back:**
- Obtain the contracts and confirm term, termination rights, and whether any amount is payable before Completion.
- Treat any portion relating to pre-Completion periods, or any non-cancellable commitment, as debt-like.

### 4.7 Office lease (DD-007)
**Seller position:** The lease imposes a notification obligation.

**Problems:** The material does not say whether landlord consent to the change of control is required.

**Push back:** Obtain a legal view and, if consent is required, make it a condition precedent to Completion. Otherwise include a specific indemnity for lease default.

### 4.8 Mossvale (DD-009)
**Seller position:** Restriction on assignment; no consent needed merely because shares are sold.

**Push back:** Obtain Mossvale's confirmation or a legal opinion that the share sale does not trigger the restriction. If there is doubt, make confirmation a condition or include a specific indemnity.

---

## 5. Tax and IP

**Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."

**Problems:** Tax and IP are high-risk areas for a business like this. The Seller's approach subjects them to the general cap, basket, and 18-month time limit, which is inadequate. Tax assessments can take years to finalise, and IP ownership gaps (as with Ironquay) may not surface for a long time.

**Push back:**
- Full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax liabilities (including any PAYG, GST, payroll tax, and payroll-related exposures), outside the cap and basket, running until 60 days after the relevant limitation period.
- Separate, longer-tail IP warranties and an IP indemnity covering ownership and infringement claims arising from pre-Completion activity.

---

## 6. Funds flow

The Seller says the funds flow reflects agreed price mechanics but does not itemise the bonuses. The Buyer should check:
- Riverlark debt (AUD 3.2m) is deducted and repaid at Completion;
- Ironquay AUD 180,000 is paid or deducted;
- Completion bonuses and on-costs are deducted or paid by the Seller;
- any supplier amounts payable before Completion are reflected;
- transaction costs are allocated correctly.

The Buyer should prepare its own funds flow from the SPA price mechanics and reconcile it against the Seller's version.

---

## 7. Quantified known exposure

| Item | Amount (AUD) | Current Seller treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3,200,000 | Post-Completion release |
| Completion bonuses | 420,000 | Excluded from funds flow |
| Ironquay SOW3 | 180,000 | Limited indemnity |
| Supplier renewals | 330,000 | "Ordinary course" |
| **Subtotal (quantified)** | **~4,130,000** | |
| Bluefen (30% revenue, ~3.6m) | Unquantified loss of value | Reasonable endeavours |
| Privacy incident | Unquantified | "Not material" |
| Lease, Mossvale | Unquantified | Notification only |
| On-costs on bonuses | Unquantified | Not addressed |

The quantified items alone exceed the Seller's general cap of AUD 4.8m when combined with any other warranty claim. The Buyer should price these items, not leave them to warranty claims.

---

## 8. Recommendations (summary)

1. **Reject general disclosure** of the data room and public registers. Require specific, fair disclosure.
2. **Narrow or delete the buyer-knowledge clause (8.3)**, and ensure known matters are covered by specific indemnities.
3. **Carve fraud out** of all limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions.
4. **Reject the universal limitation** in Clause 13. Use separate categories for general, fundamental, tax, IP, and specific indemnity claims.
5. **Fundamental and title warranties**: cap at full price, outside basket and de minimis, with a longer time limit. Verify title through ASIC, PPSR, and chain-of-title searches.
6. **General regime**: tipping basket (or a lower deductible); de minimis aggregated across related claims; 36-month time limit; general cap of 20–25% as a fallback.
7. **Bluefen**: unconditional consent with all conditions satisfied as a condition precedent, with a long-stop termination right.
8. **Riverlark**: repay at Completion through the funds flow, with payoff letter and discharge documents delivered at Completion.
9. **Ironquay**: pay or deduct the AUD 180,000; obtain a confirmatory IP assignment; replace the limited indemnity with a full specific indemnity.
10. **Bonuses and on-costs**: deduct from price or require Seller to pay before Completion.
11. **Privacy incident**: specific indemnity outside the cap; Seller-funded investigation; consider a retention or escrow; obtain privacy advice on notifiability.
12. **Supplier renewals**: review contracts; treat pre-Completion or non-cancellable amounts as debt-like.
13. **Lease and Mossvale**: obtain legal confirmation; make any required consent a condition precedent or cover by specific indemnity.
14. **Tax and IP**: full tax indemnity for pre-Completion periods; longer-tail IP warranties and IP indemnity.
15. **Funds flow**: prepare an independent funds flow from the SPA mechanics and reconcile it against the Seller's version.

**Next steps:** I recommend engaging NSW corporate counsel to review the mark-up, privacy counsel to assess the DD-006 incident, and a tax adviser to review payroll tax and superannuation on the bonuses. Please send the full SPA draft and data room documents (DD-002 to DD-012) so I can check each clause reference against the actual drafting.

## 5. Tax and IP

**Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."

**Problems:** Tax and IP are high-risk areas for a business like this. The Seller's approach subjects them to the general cap, basket, and 18-month time limit, which is inadequate. Tax assessments can take years to finalise, and IP ownership gaps (as with Ironquay) may not surface for a long time.

**Push back:**
- Full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax liabilities (including any PAYG, GST, payroll tax, and payroll-related exposures), outside the cap and basket, running until 60 days after the relevant limitation period.
- Separate, longer-tail IP warranties and an IP indemnity covering ownership and infringement claims arising from pre-Completion activity.

## 8. Recommendations (summary)

1. **Reject general disclosure** of the data room and public registers. Require specific, fair disclosure.
2. **Narrow or delete the buyer-knowledge clause (8.3)**, and ensure known matters are covered by specific indemnities.
3. **Carve fraud out** of all limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions.
4. **Reject the universal limitation** in Clause 13. Use separate categories for general, fundamental, tax, IP, and specific indemnity claims.
5. **Fundamental and title warranties**: cap at full price, outside basket and de minimis, with a longer time limit. Verify title through ASIC, PPSR, and chain-of-title searches.
6. **General regime**: tipping basket (or a lower deductible); de minimis aggregated across related claims; 36-month time limit; general cap of 20–25% as a fallback.
7. **Bluefen**: unconditional consent with all conditions satisfied as a condition precedent, with a long-stop termination right.
8. **Riverlark**: repay at Completion through the funds flow, with payoff letter and discharge documents delivered at Completion.
9. **Ironquay**: pay or deduct the AUD 180,000; obtain a confirmatory IP assignment; replace the limited indemnity with a full specific indemnity.
10. **Bonuses and on-costs**: deduct from price or require Seller to pay before Completion.
11. **Privacy incident**: specific indemnity outside the cap; Seller-funded investigation; consider a retention or escrow; obtain privacy advice on notifiability.
12. **Supplier renewals**: review contracts; treat pre-Completion or non-cancellable amounts as debt-like.
13. **Lease and Mossvale**: obtain legal confirmation; make any required consent a condition precedent or cover by specific indemnity.
14. **Tax and IP**: full tax indemnity for pre-Completion periods; longer-tail IP warranties and IP indemnity.
15. **Funds flow**: prepare an independent funds flow from the SPA mechanics and reconcile it against the Seller's version.
